sentences.text: Toxoprion is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalans.
Its name combines Greek words for "bow" and "saw," describing the unique jaw shape.
Heavily serrated teeth grew outward on the lower jaw symphysis like a rounded saw.
Unlike Helicoprion, the tooth row forms a downward curved whorl instead of coiling back.
Smaller teeth at the front were juvenile, while larger ones at the back formed in adulthood.
The shift from rounded older teeth to sharper younger ones may signal dietary changes.
The genus was described by Hay in 1909.
Fossils are found in marine strata near Eureka, Nevada.
Toxoprion belongs to the parent group Helicoprionidae.
It is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Fossils date from the Early Carboniferous to the Late Permian.
The animal lived between 298.9 and 274.4 million years ago, from the Asselian to the Kungurian stages.
